Deletes all history saved on this phone (originals and translations). Subtitles on the server are not affected.
1. What this system collects Only microphone audio and the text derived from it. No camera image, no location, no contacts, and no data from other apps.

2. Where the audio goes Your speech is uploaded in blocks from the phone microphone to your own server (never to a third-party cloud). The server writes it to an audio file used for recognition; when that file passes the limit (1 GB by default) it rotates, keeping only the newest one and overwriting the old.

3. How long the text stays Subtitle records on the server are cleaned up automatically according to the retention period (7 days by default). History on the phone (originals and translations) lives only in the app private directory, at most 200 entries, and you can clear it any time from Settings.

4. Who can see it Only the participants of your meeting can see its subtitles; administrators can see accounts and term bases and do not browse meeting content. A leaked shared key means others can push subtitles to this server, so keep it private.

5. About the public internet The current trial runs plain http (port 8788); the key and the audio travel unencrypted. TLS (https) is required before real use, otherwise do not send real meeting content over the public internet.

6. Your choice If you do not want to be recorded, do not tap Start. To delete records on the phone, use Clear records in Settings. To stop the server from keeping the subtitles of this meeting, ask the administrator to clean them up per the retention period or end the meeting.
